clue.text: Be proud to attract attention

blocks.note: first meaning: to project or jut out from a surface
second meaning: to be conspicuous or notable

explanation.surface: Advice to hold your head high and get yourself noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proud' here is the builder's sense, sticking out from a surface, not feeling pride.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both physically protruding and being conspicuous among others.

clue.text: Bench alight

blocks.note: first meaning: a long wooden seat with a high back
second meaning: to come to rest, as a bird does on a branch

explanation.walkthrough: 'Alight' looks like 'on fire' but is the verb for landing or perching.
explanation.definitionFit: A settle is a high-backed wooden bench, and to settle is to perch or come down to rest.

clue.text: Pakistani male keeps swine

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer within itself, as a container keeps its contents

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A Pakistani man who raises pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swine' is the insult, a brutish person, rather than the farm pig the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are terms of abuse for a coarse, beastly person.

clue.text: Thirsty? Slip up in attempt to get a drink

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another, the word in standing for that placement

blocks.note: thirsty means in need of a drink
a shy is a throw or attempt; this is its outside part
to err is to make a mistake
the end of shy, closing round the slip

explanation.surface: Someone parched who bungles their attempt to order a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A shy is a throw, as at a coconut shy, so an attempt; ERR goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry sherry is a fortified wine, a drink in its own right.

clue.text: Dangerous antagonist threatening person who's always right?

blocks.note: an ugly mood is a menacing one
from the shop motto that the customer is always right

explanation.surface: A shop worker faces a menacing, always-right client as an adversary.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: the shopkeeper's saying makes the buyer the one who is always right.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly customer is an idiom for a person who is formidable and nasty to deal with.

clue.text: Son, reportedly reserved in group

indicators.note: what is reported is heard spoken, so the sound of the words counts, not their spelling

blocks.note: S for son and cool for reserved, said together

explanation.surface: A boy who keeps himself to himself in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A school is a group, especially of fish or of thinkers sharing views.

clue.text: Group of singers sing mostly about love

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
about means surrounding, so the shortened word wraps round the other piece

blocks.note: chirp, as a bird sings, without its last letter
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An instruction for a choir to sing mostly about love.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised body of singers, as in a church.

clue.text: Veteran's antique stopwatch?

blocks.note: antique means very old
a stopwatch is a device for timing

explanation.surface: An ex-serviceman's prized antique stopwatch.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-timer is someone with long experience, a veteran of the scene.

clue.text: One wicket left, say - defeat must follow

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
e.g. means for example, 'say'
to stump is to baffle or defeat

explanation.surface: A cricket side with one wicket left, facing defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the wicket is three stumps; leg stump is the one on the batter's leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg stump is one of the three upright stumps forming a cricket wicket.

clue.text: Three-wheeler could make short journey round

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: trip, a journey, without its final letter
a cycle is a round, as of events

explanation.surface: A child on a three-wheeler could manage a short trip round the block.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricycle is a pedal vehicle with three wheels.

clue.text: Heated chow?

blocks.note: surface reading: food (chow) that has been warmed up
setter's reading: a chow is a breed of dog, so a heated chow is a warm dog

explanation.walkthrough: Chow is both slang for food and a Chinese breed of dog; both readings land on the same snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot dog is a sausage in a bun, food served warm.

clue.text: With a good chance of winning at home, struggle

definitions.text: With a good chance of winning

blocks.note: someone at home is in
contention is strife or dispute

explanation.surface: A sports team playing at home, battling with a real shot at victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in contention means being among those still able to win a contest.

clue.text: Lead found amongst Wensleydale - a sheepdog's

indicators.note: the answer is discovered sitting among the letters of the following words

blocks.note: runs across the end of the place name, the article and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A sheepdog's lead turns up somewhere in the Yorkshire Dales.
explanation.walkthrough: Wensleydale is a valley in Yorkshire, northern England, known for sheep and cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead is the strap used to hold a dog, the same as a leash.

clue.text: A swindler, in contrast, I suspect

indicators.note: as an adjective suspect means dodgy or unreliable, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order

blocks.note: the word and the pronoun together supply the letters

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a fraudster is, by contrast, behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A con artist is a confidence trickster, one who cheats people out of money.

clue.text: Drink port, the best

blocks.note: Bristol is a port city in south-west England
the cream is the finest part

explanation.surface: Instruction to drink port, the finest one available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts as the drink, but it is the harbour city; the drink is the definition word at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol Cream is a well-known brand of sweet sherry, a drink.

clue.text: Applicant outspoken at start of exchange

indicators.note: the start of a word means only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: candid means frank, speaking plainly
taken as written
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A job applicant who speaks bluntly from the outset of an interview exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is someone applying for a job or standing for office.

clue.text: Exact remedy

blocks.note: first meaning: precise, particular
second meaning: a medicine aimed at one particular disease

explanation.walkthrough: The noun sense, a drug targeted at a single complaint, is old-fashioned but in the dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means precise and clearly defined, and as a noun it names a cure for one ailment.

clue.text: Two brutes with it, hit man

blocks.note: an ass is a stupid beast, and two of them
in means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: Two thugs, cool and trendy, call in a hired killer.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a killer of a prominent person, often paid like a hit man.

clue.text: Cat by track moving stealthily

blocks.note: pussy is a familiar word for a cat
footing is a foothold, the ground one treads on

explanation.surface: A cat creeping along beside a path.
explanation.definitionFit: Pussyfooting means treading cautiously and softly, as a cat does when stalking.

clue.text: Dexterous with it, a rod at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and disordered, so these letters lose their order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: An angler handling a fishing rod skilfully out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and quick, especially with the hands.

clue.text: Girl in bedroom making flag

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, as someone is inside a room

blocks.note: BR is the estate-agent abbreviation for bedroom
a common girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl in her bedroom making a flag for a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: The bedroom abbreviation comes from property listings for homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner is a flag or long strip of cloth bearing a device or slogan.

clue.text: Lizard caught by hole - name's peculiar

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, out of the normal arrangement, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the two words supply the letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: A lizard trapped in a hole whose name is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the abbreviation next to the reordered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The chameleon is a lizard known for changing colour.

clue.text: Tennis champion always last to protest

indicators.note: last picks out only the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: ever means always
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tennis star who is always the last one to complain.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Evert is the American tennis player who won 18 Grand Slam singles titles.
explanation.definitionFit: Evert was a dominant women's tennis champion of the 1970s and 1980s.

clue.text: Country home rejected financial assistance perhaps

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: at home means in
aid is help, financial or otherwise

explanation.surface: A nation that turned down overseas financial aid.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a country in South Asia.

clue.text: Promote nurse

blocks.note: first meaning: to encourage the growth of
second meaning: to bring up a child that is not one's own

explanation.walkthrough: Both words are verbs here, though 'nurse' reads first as the hospital worker.
explanation.definitionFit: To foster is both to encourage the development of something and to care for a child as a guardian.

clue.text: Dance from musical (not British)

indicators.note: not British means the abbreviation for British is taken away

blocks.note: Brigadoon is a Lerner and Loewe stage musical
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A dance number taken from a stage show, minus the British production.
explanation.walkthrough: Brigadoon is a 1947 musical about a vanishing Scottish village; dropping its B leaves the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigadoon is a lively old dance for couples, of French origin.

clue.text: Shrewd capturing an English king

indicators.note: capturing means taking hold of and enclosing, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: cute can mean clever or sharp-witted
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clever plot to seize an English monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Cute in the sense of shrewd is older and mostly American.
explanation.definitionFit: Canute (Cnut) was a Danish king who ruled England in the eleventh century.

clue.text: Pangolin seen in tent area, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so these letters may be reordered

blocks.note: the letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: A pangolin spotted around the campsite.
explanation.definitionFit: The pangolin is also called the scaly anteater, since it lives on ants and termites.
